title: At low contractility (rho*=0.2) with weak noise, a uniformly polarized round cell breaks symmetry by itself and becomes a half-moon crawler
summary: Same Camley world (world.py, per-body pool), but rho*=0.2 instead of 0.4, started as a round cell with rho high everywhere (ffrac=1). With ongoing noise eta=2 on rho, the disk swells. When the high state reaches 1/2 (t~1.5), the uniform state becomes the unstable middle root; one side drops low, the other stays high, and the cell crawls as a half-moon at 0.42 to t=12 (uniform_rs02_eta2.png). Without noise the same disk swells, switches to the low state everywhere at once, retracts and vanishes by t~4.5 (uniform_rs02_eta0.png). At rho*=0.4, uniform-high disks are stable and static, which is the dead end that front cuts reach in 20261025T1915-c22-wavepin-front-cut-no-repair. A polarized start at rho*=0.2 also crawls (0.44, polarized_rs02_eta0.png). One seed each; probe images, not packs.
